grh_f94cca62257e707156bc.title: The Liar
paragraphs: Lydia Parker returns to Rivers End after years away and asks Dr. Christian for help with her twin sister Lucy. Lydia says Lucy has become a compulsive liar, inventing pointless stories about where she has been, what she has done and whom she has seen, and that the behavior has worsened since the death of Lucy's husband Emil. Christian listens carefully as Lydia describes their lifelong closeness and insists that Lucy is physically healthy but emotionally disturbed. He suggests rest and familiar surroundings and avoids directly challenging Lydia's account. Only after Lydia leaves again, supposedly taking Lucy to relatives in California, does the truth emerge: Lucy died of pneumonia in the spring of 1901, nearly forty years earlier, and Christian himself was a pallbearer at her funeral. Lydia never accepted her twin's death and has continued to live as though Lucy were beside her, creating new stories to explain her supposed activities. Because Lydia remains harmless and otherwise functions normally, Christian chooses compassion over a brutal confrontation with the fantasy, arguing that the lonely woman's private reality deserves understanding rather than ridicule.

Credited performers include Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Production credits include announcer Bob Anderson.
The surviving audio runs about 25 minutes. Sponsor associations in the structured record include [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_f96db23fed406e877db1.title: Mr and Mrs Smith
paragraphs: David and Ann Smith learn that a legal technicality means their three-year marriage was never valid. David assumes they will simply marry again, but Ann is furious when he treats the situation casually and decides to make him earn her back. She begins seeing David's law partner Jefferson, whose courtly Southern manners give David a very real rival. The contest follows them to a winter resort, where Ann stages one last attempt to make David give up on her and David refuses to be driven away. Their jealousy finally exposes that neither wants anyone else, and the Smiths reconcile as a couple all over again.
